question: Consider matrices $A$ and $B$, both $3 \times 3$ and non-singular. Prove that $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$. Then, if $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, compute $(AB)^{-1}$.
explanation:
(i) Conceptual Proof:
$(AB)(B^{-1}A^{-1}) = A(B B^{-1})A^{-1} = A I A^{-1} = A A^{-1} = I$
Similarly, $(B^{-1}A^{-1})(AB) = B^{-1}(A^{-1}A)B = B^{-1}I B = B^{-1}B = I$
Thus, $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$

(ii) Compute $A^{-1}$ and $B^{-1}$

Step 1: Find $|A|$ and adj $A$

$|A| = 2\begin{vmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} - 1\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{vmatrix}$
$= 2(12-0) - 1(0-1) = 24 + 1 = 25$

Compute minors/cofactors for adj $A$:
E.g., $C_{11} = \begin{vmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4\end{vmatrix} = 12-0=12$
$C_{12} = -\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{vmatrix} = -(0-1) = 1$
$C_{13} = \begin{vmatrix}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} = 0-3=-3$
Continue for all...

Collect cofactors, construct adj $A$, $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{25} (\text{adj }A)$
Do similar computation for $B$, with $|B| = ...$
B is upper-triangular so $|B| = 1 \times 1 \times 1 = 1$

Find adj $B$, $B^{-1}$ using minors/cofactors.

Finally, $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$
Calculate $A^{-1}, B^{-1}$ explicitly, multiply to obtain $(AB)^{-1}$.
